_readme.purpose: Reproducibility record for the rooftop city asset set.
_readme.world: js/config/city.js is the contract. Every asset here fills a declared slot; run `npm run assets` for what is still outstanding.
_readme.tool: Codex CLI with the openai/skills imagegen skill, built-in image_gen mode (ChatGPT auth, no OPENAI_API_KEY).
_readme.style_reference: assets/city/master_rooftop.png for every prop; that master was itself generated with style.PNG attached as a treatment reference.
_readme.sheet_strategy: Every prop is generated as part of a SHEET rather than alone. A row of props made together shares one lighting setup and one palette, so they belong to each other before they ever reach the engine; generated one at a time they drift and the roof stops reading as one place.

shared_clauses.camera: STRAIGHT ON FROM THE SIDE at eye level - not from above, not isometric, no perspective tilt. The game camera looks horizontally.
shared_clauses.ground: Every object sits flat on an imaginary ground line at the SAME height across the row, so the engine can place them on a floor.
shared_clauses.separation: All props clearly SEPARATED with a wide clear gap of empty background between each so they never touch. Touching props defeat the splitter.
shared_clauses.background: A FLAT PURE WHITE (#FFFFFF) background, completely uniform. CRITICAL: crisp well defined edges where each object meets the white - no glow, no bloom, no haze bleeding outward, NO GROUND SHADOW, no floor, no ground plane.
shared_clauses.no_shadow_why: Ground shadows are excluded deliberately: the engine draws contact shadows itself so they respond to depth and elevation. A painted shadow would double up and sit at the wrong angle.
shared_clauses.style: Painterly stylized rendering matching assets/city/master_rooftop.png exactly - soft simplified forms, hand-painted surfaces, no crisp vector edges, no photorealism. Deep indigo and violet night palette with warm amber practicals.

pipeline: Generate the sheet to assets/city/raw/ - NEVER to a processed path. A background generator finishing late will overwrite whatever sits at its output path, which silently destroyed processed layers earlier in this project.

Check the transparency PERCENTAGE, not just the mode, before keying. One sheet came back RGBA at 0% transparent (white background in an alpha-capable file); another came back with real alpha, and keying it as white-backed deleted the artwork.
For tiling layers: python scripts/tile.py fix in.png out.png --blend 0.05
house_rules: Ask for flat pure white, not transparency. The model returns RGB without alpha more often than not, and a flat white key is deterministic to remove.
cutout tolerance 40 + erode 1. Tolerance 70 leaks through anti-aliased edges into light artwork and destroys the sprite.

--pockets is MANDATORY on prop sheets. Enclosed background the border fill cannot reach - between bench slats, under a railing, between leaves - survives as solid white blocks. It needs its own much tighter tolerance (~30) than the border fill, because the border fill stops at the first out-of-range pixel while a global colour test does not.

Demand a WIDE clearly empty gap between props in the prompt. Touching props defeat the splitter; the character sheet needed valley-splitting and largest-blob cleanup the first time because frames touched.
-i is variadic and swallows a positional prompt; pass prompts on stdin.
No ground shadows, no ground plane, no sky, no city behind - the engine draws contact shadows itself so they respond to depth and elevation. A painted shadow doubles up and sits at the wrong angle.
Keep lit props DIM in the asset. neon_sign came back at lum 162 against a master of 29; the engine adds the glow additively on top, which is what lets the neon flicker.

art_direction.decision: The world is PIXEL ART. An earlier pass generated painterly props and quantised them; that produced soft, muddy sprites that did not sit with a pixel character. Every asset was regenerated as pixel art from the start.
art_direction.pixel_clause:
CRITICAL STYLE - authentic hand-made pixel art, like a 16-bit era game:
- chunky deliberate pixels with hard edges, NO anti-aliasing, NO soft gradients, NO blur, NO painterly brushwork
- a strictly LIMITED palette: about 4 to 6 flat colours per material, hard-edged shading bands, never smooth shading
- simplified readable forms, no fine rendered detail, no photographic texture
- crisp single-pixel rim light on top and back edges
- strong readable silhouettes that stay clear at small size
- where a gradient is needed, use DITHERING: a checkerboard of two flat colours, exactly as a 16-bit artist would, never a smooth blend
art_direction.measured_finding: Asking for pixel art does NOT produce true pixel art. The generated 'pixel art' sheets still measure ~80,000 unique colours with no detectable pixel grid (strongest block candidate scores ~1.10, i.e. noise). The generator produces the LOOK; the quantisation pass is what makes it real. Both halves are required: art designed as a sprite quantises cleanly, a photoreal render turns to mush.
art_direction.style_reference_note: style.PNG - the user's original reference - is NOT pixel art either: 87,929 unique colours in 603x232 and no grid at any block size. It was used for treatment and mood only.

quantisation.grid: scripts/pixelate.py --block 2 for props and the character, --block 2 for layers. Box-filtered down so blocks average rather than sampling one arbitrary pixel.
quantisation.palette: assets/city/palette.json - 64 colours, every asset snapped to it. Built from 8 sources sampled EQUALLY (60k px each). Concatenating raw pixels weights by area, so a full-frame skyline drowned out the props and produced 0 warm slots in 64 - a wooden crate came out purple.
quantisation.accents: 9 colours appended by hand on top of the derived ramp: lamp core, amber falloff, deep amber, highlight, neon cyan, cold window, neon magenta, greenhouse green, aircraft red. A median-cut of a 91%-shadow night scene has no room for the few bright colours the eye actually goes to.
quantisation.engine: ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false, reset after every setTransform - the DPR transform silently re-enables smoothing and resamples the pixels away.

master_rooftop.role: Style bible for the whole set. Every prop sheet is generated with this attached; it is never drawn in the game.
master_rooftop.reference_image: style.PNG (treatment only - painterly surfaces, haze, bloom, ~40% silhouette, coloured shadows, dark exposure)

measured.note: Darker than style.PNG (84 / 43%) because it is night rather than sunset. Three tone variants were produced in _tone_compare.png; no lift has been applied to the master.

sky.prompt_summary: Night sky only. Indigo to midnight gradient, darker at top, hazier and warmer toward the horizon. Faint stars, thin violet and cyan cloud bands, no moon. Bottom quarter soft luminous haze because the skyline covers it.
sky.stylecheck: lum 32, sat 0.86, shadow R-B -34 -> ok against the master

skyline.prompt_summary: Dense night skyline receding into haze, grids of tiny lit windows, soft neon blooms, red aircraft lights, masts and water tanks breaking the roofline. Top third fully transparent. Seamless left-to-right tiling demanded explicitly.

deck.prompt_summary: Flat rooftop deck surface, worn concrete and asphalt, tar seams, shallow puddles catching blue and amber. Completely flat and unobstructed because the character walks its whole length and props are placed separately. Seamless tiling demanded.
deck.stylecheck: lum 35, sat 0.68 -> flagged 'washed out, shadow hue off'; bluer than the master. Left as-is because the per-plane haze unifies it in situ.

sheet_structures.role: The five enterable structures, one per portfolio section. Largest things on screen, so they anchor the composition.
contents: 1 brick stairwell hut, pitched roof, warm glowing open doorway, lamp above, ivy
2 concrete utility shed, corrugated roof, warm square window, rusted conduit
3 corrugated metal shack, roll-up shutter part open, light spilling underneath
4 glass greenhouse, pitched glazing, glowing soft green from within, cracked panes
5 radio mast: equipment cabin plus steel lattice tower, red warning lamp, guy wires
sheet_structures.split_command: python scripts/split_sheet.py <cut> assets/city/props stair_hut utility_shed corrugated_shack greenhouse radio_mast
sheet_structures.note: Painterly generation, replaced by the pixel-art version. Kept for the record; the shipped asset is the _px one.

sheet_content.role: The portfolio itself, as objects. Each opens a panel: the terminal, three projects, the resume, the blog stack and the guestbook.
contents: 1 CRT monitor on a milk crate, green glowing screen, trailing cables
2 open laptop on a low stool, pale blue screen
3 electronics prototype board on a trestle, small red and amber LEDs
4 weathered blank poster on a leaning plywood board, curling edges
5 clipboard with a thick stack of papers, propped against a crate
6 newsstand rack holding folded blank newspapers
7 cast iron mailbox on a post, flag up, envelopes in the slot
sheet_content.split_command: python scripts/split_sheet.py <cut> assets/city/props crt_terminal laptop prototype_board poster clipboard newsstand mailbox
sheet_content.note: Painterly generation, replaced by the pixel-art version. Kept for the record; the shipped asset is the _px one.

sheet_clutter.role: Scattered density. Placed by the seeded scatter() in city.js - 9 assets become roughly 60 instances spread across x and depth.
contents: 1 air-conditioning condenser, fan grille, rusted casing
2 stack of three wooden crates, askew
3 terracotta planter with a scruffy shrub
4 cluster of galvanised vent pipes, mushroom caps
5 rectangular ducting on short legs, taped seam
6 pile of damp sagging cardboard boxes
7 folded metal folding chair, side on
8 clump of weeds through a crack
9 shallow puddle seen almost edge on, wider than tall, amber and cyan reflection
sheet_clutter.split_command: python scripts/split_sheet.py <cut> assets/city/props ac_unit crates planter vent_pipes duct boxes folding_chair weed puddle
sheet_clutter.note: Painterly generation, replaced by the pixel-art version. Kept for the record; the shipped asset is the _px one.

_outstanding.all: NONE. 260/260 slots; 121 assets, every one on-palette.

sheet_structures_px.role: The five enterable structures, one per portfolio section.
sheet_structures_px.prompt_note: Pixel clause + five structures side on, lit windows and doorways as FLAT BLOCKS of warm amber rather than glows, all on one ground line, wide gaps.
sheet_structures_px.split: python scripts/split_sheet.py <cut> assets/city/pixel stair_hut utility_shed corrugated_shack greenhouse radio_mast

sheet_content_px.role: The portfolio as objects - terminal, three projects, resume, blog stack, guestbook.
sheet_content_px.prompt_note: Pixel clause + seven interactables side on, screens as flat blocks of colour, explicitly no readable text anywhere.
sheet_content_px.split: python scripts/split_sheet.py <cut> assets/city/pixel crt_terminal laptop prototype_board poster clipboard newsstand mailbox

sheet_clutter_px.role: Scattered density. 9 assets become ~60 instances via the seeded scatter() in city.js.
sheet_clutter_px.split: python scripts/split_sheet.py <cut> assets/city/pixel ac_unit crates planter vent_pipes duct boxes folding_chair weed puddle

sheet_tall_px.role: Middle-distance structures on the 'far' plane, read mostly as dark shapes with rim light.
sheet_tall_px.split: python scripts/split_sheet.py <cut> assets/city/pixel water_tower water_tank_small chimney satellite_dish antenna neon_sign laundry_line

sheet_viewpoint.role: The stargazing viewpoint at the far end of the roof, plus the coop and vending machine.
sheet_viewpoint.split: python scripts/split_sheet.py <cut> assets/city/pixel telescope bench railing pigeon_coop vending_machine bulb_string
sheet_viewpoint.note: Bench and railing came back with solid cream blocks between the slats and under the rail - the case that made --pockets mandatory.

sheet_foreground.role: The 'fore' plane, drawn in front of the character at parallax 1.4 and darkened 0.45 by the engine, so they read as near-silhouette.
sheet_foreground.prompt_note: Pixel clause + three pieces rooted at the bottom edge, very dark bodies with only a thin cool rim light. The parapet must tile seamlessly.
sheet_foreground.split: python scripts/split_sheet.py <cut> assets/city/pixel parapet fore_plant fore_pipe
sheet_foreground.tiling: parapet measured 0.0 edge mismatch after tile.py fix --blend 0.08

layers_px.role: The three backdrops, regenerated as pixel art.
layers_px.note: sky and deck were generated as TWO BANDS STACKED VERTICALLY in one image with a white gap between them, then split on that gap - it keeps their palettes identical. The sky uses dithered checkerboard bands instead of a smooth gradient, which is the 16-bit solution to a gradient and had to be asked for explicitly.
layers_px.manifest_change: The new deck plate is a shallower band, so backdrops.deck heightFrac went 0.30 -> 0.34 to keep the horizon where the layout expects it.

character_px.role: Player character: 4-frame idle + 8-frame walk, side profile facing right. Walking left is Sprite.flipX, mirrored at draw time about the pivot.
character_px.prompt_note: Pixel clause + explicit face direction. The first pixel character had large dark eyes that read as hollow and unsettling at sprite size; the reroll demands the face be almost entirely implied - no large eyes, no dark sockets, no pupils, no mouth, at most a single soft dot close to skin tone, with hair covering most of the head.
pipeline: slice columns 0-3 to idle, 4-11 to walk
pixelate --block 2  (block 3 cost the silhouette its hair and boots)
character_px.verified: 0px baseline drift on both clips, 0-0.5px centre spread. 12 frames separated by gap detection alone, no valley-splitting fallback needed.

sheet_skyline_px.role: The horizon city on the 'skyline' plane. Added because the upper half of the frame measured 48% empty and both the sky and skyline planes carried ZERO props while the deck carried 64. These are the tallest things in the world and exist to put something above the midline.
sheet_skyline_px.prompt_note: Pixel clause + four distant night-city structures in one row: a plain office slab, a stepped-setback block, a taller art-deco tower with a spire, and a tower crane for the one diagonal. Near-silhouette dark blue-grey, thin cool rim light down one vertical edge, and only a DOZEN sparse warm windows each - not a lit grid. Explicitly asked for the deco tower to be tallest.
sheet_skyline_px.background: flat pure white; came back RGB, 0% transparent, 82% within tolerance of the corner - the documented white-backed case
sheet_skyline_px.split: python scripts/split_sheet.py <cut> assets/city/pixel sky_tower_a sky_tower_b sky_tower_c sky_crane
sheet_skyline_px.stylecheck: lum 22-28 against a master of 29; all four ok, no grading needed
sheet_skyline_px.placement_note: MIND THE PARALLAX. The skyline plane runs at 0.25, so it only sweeps parallax*maxScroll past the window: usable x is about [0, 2550]. Three FAR-plane props (chimney_d, dish_c, laundry) had been authored at deck-like x of 4550-5450 and could never be seen at any window size. tests/Composition.test.js now guards this.

sheet_sky_px.role: The 'sky' plane, which had no props at all. A moon to anchor the upper frame and two night clouds.
sheet_sky_px.background: FLAT PURE MAGENTA (#FF00FF), NOT white - and this matters. The moon is pale cream and the clouds are light-edged; a white key would have eaten them. cutout.py seeds its flood from the top-left PIXEL, not from white, so any uniform colour works. Came back RGB, 0% transparent, 93% near-corner. Use magenta for any pale sheet.
sheet_sky_px.split: python scripts/split_sheet.py <cut> assets/city/pixel moon cloud_a cloud_b
sheet_sky_px.stylecheck: moon lum 197, clouds 42-45, all flagged against a master of 29 - and all three kept as-is. The moon is a LIGHT SOURCE, not a lit prop: every colour in it is on the 64 palette (which reaches lum 246 precisely because of the hand-added bright accents), so the art stands and the engine's additive glow was dropped from 0.42 to 0.26 instead. Clouds catching city glow are legitimately lighter than a roof.

sheet_farprops_px.role: Middle-distance fillers for the bare stretches on the 'far' plane, plus the pole the rooftop bulb strings hang from.
sheet_farprops_px.prompt_note: Billboard face explicitly BLANK - no text, no logo - and explicitly dim, because the engine lights it.
sheet_farprops_px.grade: far_tower and utility_pole: grade --strength 0.6 (cast only; they came back at shadow R-B -15 against the reference -29). far_billboard: grade --strength 0.5 --exposure 0.5, taking it from lum 103 to 34.
sheet_farprops_px.pipeline_order: split -> grade -> pixelate, and pixelate EXACTLY ONCE. `pixelate --apply` halves the resolution every time it runs; running it twice quietly shipped far_billboard at half its intended size.

cable_run_px.role: Power lines tiling the length of the world on the 'far' plane. One horizontal drawn across the emptiest part of the frame.
cable_run_px.tiling: Generated with a pole at each edge, but the poles came back INSET (x 89-138 and 1635-1684 of 1774). Tiling that clusters the poles in pairs at every seam. Cropped pole-centre to pole-centre (113..1659) so each tile is one span and the two half-poles join into one; tile.py check then reports 3.1/255.
cable_run_px.pockets_note: --pockets is what makes this asset work at all. The four cables plus the poles ENCLOSE the background between them, which the border flood cannot reach. Without it the sheet came out at lum 194 - white trapped between the wires - against a master of 29. With it, 23 and 'ok'. Same 78.3% border-clear figure either way, so the printed percentage does NOT tell you whether pockets ran.
cable_run_px.file_note: Came back RGBA at 0% transparent - the documented alpha-capable-but-white-backed trap. Checked the percentage, not the mode.

sheet_comfort_px.role: Furnishing the LOOKOUT, which measured the sparsest zone on the roof (8.1 props/1000px against the workshop's 16) while being the largest at 1600px. Prompted as a sitting area rather than as clutter: the workshop end is where work happens, this end is where you stop.
sheet_comfort_px.grade: --strength 0.5, cast only. All six came back 'ok'.

sheet_rooffurniture_px.role: Height. The deck's median prop was 81px with 50 of 68 under 100, so away from the five structures the roof was a flat line of ankle-height clutter. pigeon_loft is also the POST zone's landmark - it explains the pigeons and the mail that zone is about, so the prop that fixes the composition also explains the space.
sheet_rooffurniture_px.pockets_note: Mandatory here: the guyed antenna's wires enclose two large triangles the border flood cannot reach.

sheet_foreground2_px.role: The fore plane was 9 props from THREE unique images across 6200px, which is why every frame read flat - nothing for the camera to look past.
sheet_foreground2_px.grade: --strength 0.7 --exposure 0.75, taking them to lum 11-13. Foreground sits closest to the camera and should read as shape, not detail.
sheet_foreground2_px.rejected: A hanging cable swag was tried on this plane and dropped. tests/Scale.test.js requires every fore prop to be rooted at y 1.0, and it is right: at parallax 1.4 anything not rooted at the bottom sweeps across mid-frame faster than the roof moves, which reads as an object sliding rather than as depth. Cables live on `far`.

interiors_px.role: The two interiors. Prompted per ROOM rather than per object, so each sheet shares one lighting setup: the workshop warm and amber under one bulb, the stairwell cold, grey-green and institutional. The rooms have to disagree with each other — one is worked in, the other is only passed through.
interiors_px.exposure_note: Interiors sit ABOVE the night-roof master by design, and stylecheck will always call them washed out; that is the right verdict for a lit room measured against an outdoor night scene. What is NOT fine is running away from it: plans came back at lum 116, stair_wall at 115, noticeboard 73. Graded per asset to land in 19-48, with stair_window highest at 48 because it is a lit window. A BACKDROP must end up darker than the props standing in front of it, or they read as silhouettes against a glowing wall.
interiors_px.tiling: The four layers go through tile.py fix, not cutout — they are full-frame textures with no background to key. ws_wall came back at 25.1/255 and st_floor at 19.8; fix took all four to 0.0, and they stay under 0.4 after grading and pixelating.
interiors_px.parapet_fix: parapet.png had been shipping with 446 colours, 405 of them off-palette (3.65% of its pixels — an unsnapped anti-aliased fringe). `pixelate --apply --block 1` snaps colour WITHOUT halving the resolution: 343x177 preserved, 42 colours, 0 off-palette. Use --block 1 to re-snap an existing asset.

sheet_cat_px.role: The roof's cat. THREE STATIC POSES, not an animated sheet: a multi-frame walk cycle from an image model drifts between frames (the character sheet needed repack and compose to survive it), and at this size a cat reads almost entirely from its silhouette. The engine swaps the pose.
sheet_cat_px.prompt_note: Asked for the SAME animal three times - same size, same markings, pale chest patch - and for the face to be almost implied, the lesson from the first pixel character whose large dark eyes read as hollow. All three face right; left is mirrored at draw time.

sheet_roofstuff_px.role: Signs that somebody comes up here on purpose. The roof had plenty of ducts and crates and no evidence of a person; these are things left rather than installed.
sheet_roofstuff_px.pockets_note: Mandatory: the bicycle's spoked wheels are dozens of enclosed pockets the border flood cannot reach.

city_bands_px.role: The background city, in three parallax bands. One skyline plane gives the background a single distance, so it reads as a painted flat however many towers are on it; three bands let buildings pass each other as the camera moves, which is what says 'miles of city'.
city_bands_px.prompt_note: Varying the SILHOUETTE was stated as mattering more than the detail, because these are read as shapes on a horizon. Signs were told to carry no letters or text of any kind - a generated word in the background is a distraction and usually misspelt. Everything lit was told to stay dim; the engine adds the glow.
city_bands_px.animation: sky_neon palette-cycles, beacon_mast and tower_mast pulse as aircraft warning lights, sky_flue and far_vent_cluster smoke through the declared-emitter system the roof's own vents use.
city_bands_px.stylecheck: all sixteen 'ok' at lum 19-29 against a master of 29, graded --strength 0.5 for cast only.

front_lip_px.role: The depth band nearest the camera held SEVEN of the deck's hundred props while being the largest area on screen, which is why the bottom of the frame read empty however much went on the roof behind it.
front_lip_px.grade: The lip objects came back at lum 37-55 and were graded per asset to 27-30 against a master of 29. The three foreground pieces went to lum 7 with --strength 0.7 --exposure 0.75: the foreground is read as shape, not detail.
front_lip_px.note: Most of the new density is SCATTERED FROM EXISTING IMAGES, not generated. Down at the lip the eye wants repetition; sixteen more generations would have been the wrong answer. `npm run assets` caught one wrong path where a scatter pointed at `interior/offcuts.png` - a warm-bulb-lit asset that would have read wrong against a night roof.
